title: Tensor kernel of a leg in a two-summand exact presentation
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $P,Q,Q',E,L$ be $R$-modules, and let $a:P\to Q$ and $b:P\to Q'$ be linear maps. Put $D=Q'\oplus Q$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], $\delta(x)=(b(x),-a(x))$, and let $\pi:D\to E$ be a surjective linear map with $\ker\pi=\operatorname{im}\delta$. Set $\iota_1(y)=(y,0)$, $\iota_2(z)=(0,z)$ and $j=\pi\iota_1$. For every linear map $h$ write $h_L=h\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L$, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. There are mutually inverse linear maps $F:D\otimes_RL\to(Q'\otimes_RL)\oplus(Q\otimes_RL)$ and $G$ characterized by $F((y,z)\otimes l)=(y\otimes l,z\otimes l)$ and $G(s,t)=(\iota_1)_L(s)+(\iota_2)_L(t)$. They satisfy $F\delta_L(w)=(b_L(w),-a_L(w))$ and $\pi_LG(s,0)=j_L(s)$. Moreover $\pi_L$ is surjective, $\ker\pi_L=\operatorname{im}\delta_L$, and
$$\ker j_L=b_L(\ker a_L)=\{b_L(w):w\in P\otimes_RL,\ a_L(w)=0\}.$$
These assertions hold for arbitrary $L$, without any flatness hypothesis or injectivity hypothesis on $a$, $b$ or $\delta$.

source.place: Tag 0AUM, lemma-domination-universally-injective, proof: tensoring the quotient pushout and its kernel sequence; Tag 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact, for right exactness.

proof.text: For two summands, the componentwise definition [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] identifies $D=Q'\oplus Q$ with the product $Q'\times Q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product] to these two modules and $N=L$. It gives the linear isomorphism $F$ with the required pure-tensor formula. Define the linear map $G(s,t)=(\iota_1)_L(s)+(\iota_2)_L(t)$, using the induced linear maps of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. On pairs $(y\otimes l,0)$ and $(0,z\otimes l)$ its composite with $F$ is the identity; these pairs generate the target. Conversely, $GF((y,z)\otimes l)=(y,0)\otimes l+(0,z)\otimes l=(y,z)\otimes l$. Pure tensors generate the source, so $GF=1$ and $FG=1$. Thus $G=F^{-1}$; the generation statement also proves uniqueness of the maps characterized in the item.

proof.text: For $w=x\otimes l$ the definitions give $F\delta_L(w)=(b(x)\otimes l,-a(x)\otimes l)=(b_L(w),-a_L(w))$. Both sides are linear in $w$, so equality holds for all $w\in P\otimes_RL$ by pure-tensor generation [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Since $G(s,0)=(\iota_1)_L(s)$, functoriality from that same definition gives $\pi_LG(s,0)=(\pi\iota_1)_L(s)=j_L(s)$ for every $s$.

source.place: Tag 0AUM, lemma-domination-universally-injective, tensor-pushout paragraph: explicit coordinates; Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property.

proof.text: The hypotheses on $\pi$ say exactly that $P\xrightarrow{\delta}D\xrightarrow{\pi}E\to0$ is right exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] with $(M_1,M_2,M_3,N)=(P,D,E,L)$ and $(f,g)=(\delta,\pi)$. It yields surjectivity of $\pi_L$ and $\ker\pi_L=\operatorname{im}\delta_L$. Its hypotheses ask for surjectivity of $\pi$ and the stated kernel equality, both given, and impose neither flatness of $L$ nor injectivity of $\delta$.

source.place: Tag 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact; applied to the presentation of Tag 0AUM (lemma-domination-universally-injective).

proof.text: Let $s\in\ker j_L$. Step 2 gives $G(s,0)\in\ker\pi_L$. The right-exact kernel equality of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], applied in Step 3, supplies $w\in P\otimes_RL$ with $\delta_L(w)=G(s,0)$. Applying $F$ and using Steps 1 and 2 gives $(b_L(w),-a_L(w))=(s,0)$, hence $b_L(w)=s$ and $a_L(w)=0$. This proves $\ker j_L\subseteq b_L(\ker a_L)$. Conversely, if $a_L(w)=0$, Step 2 gives $F\delta_L(w)=(b_L(w),0)$; applying the inverse $G$ yields $\delta_L(w)=G(b_L(w),0)$. Therefore $j_L(b_L(w))=\pi_LG(b_L(w),0)=\pi_L\delta_L(w)=0$, the last equality following from the exactness in Step 3. Both inclusions hold for the arbitrary module $L$, and prove the asserted equality and its displayed set description.
